paragraphs: R’ Yaakov, son of Yaakov’s daughter.

Hyman cites Eruvin 80b. In the matching passage at [80a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.80a.11-12), R’ Zeira told him, “When you reach there (the Land of Israel), make a detour and go to the Ladder of Tyre, and ask R’ Yaakov bar Idi.” When he reached there, he asked him. [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Eruvin.80a.11.1) explains that his father was not worthy, so his name was not mentioned.

In [Maaser Sheni, chapter 5, halakhah 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Maaser_Sheni.5.1.6), R’ Berechyah cites R’ Yaakov, son of Yaakov’s daughter, who in turn cites R’ Chanina of Berat Chavran. He is mentioned in [Shabbat 149b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.149b.5-6). Hyman says that [Yalkut Tehillim, remez 630](https://www.sefaria.org/Yalkut_Shimoni_on_Nach.630), copied the statement as R’ Yaakov bar Yaakov and that it SHOULD READ “son of Yaakov’s daughter.”[^4]

notes.text: The matching journey instruction is on the checked Eruvin 80a, while Hyman supplies 80b. The heading and later correction explicitly mean Yaakov’s daughter’s son. תר״ל is 630, not the earlier note’s 830.

No new primary scalar was returned. The maternal relationship is precisely son of Yaakov’s daughter. The earlier Eruvin80a comparison remains beside supplied80b, not a new whole-folio inspection. Hyman attributes the father-unworthiness explanation to Rashi and says the Yalkut reading SHOULD READ the daughter’s-son form. Remez תר״ל is630, not830; Berat Chavran retains its resh. These are source accounts, not identity or family adjudications. Uninspected abbreviated personal titles remain R-prime.

The printed locator is Eruvin 80b (vol. II, p. 778). In the consulted Eruvin 80a, R’ Zeira directs Yaakov, the daughter’s son, to Rav Yaakov bar Idi, and the following passage gives the question he asked. Rashi explicitly explains the omission of the father’s name. In the consulted Jerusalem Talmud Maaser Sheni 5:1, the corresponding report names Chunya of Berat Chavran, and the next chain names Chananyah separately. The corresponding saying in Shabbat 149b names the daughter’s son. The digital Yalkut, remez 630, reads Yaakov bar Yaakov, the reading that Hyman proposes to correct.

The corresponding [Seder HaDorot entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2105&lang=en) cites Eruvin 80a and Shabbat 149b and gives the name Chunya of Hauran in the Jerusalem Talmud chain.
